title: Emergent Electronic Bond-Order Wave in a Quasi-One-Dimensional Chain
authors: Honghao Wang, Tristan R. Cao, Pedro Schlottmann, Gang Cao
abstract: Collective order is notoriously difficult to stabilize in one dimension, where strong fluctuations suppress symmetry-breaking states. Here we report the emergence of an electronic bond-order wave (BOW) in the quasi-one-dimensional (1D) material Ba9Rh8O24, in which structural bonds become active electronic degrees of freedom that overcome 1D fluctuations to establish long-range order. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction uncovers a striking inversion of inequivalent Rh-Rh bonds across a transition TA = 180 K, where short and long bonds interchange their identities rather than undergoing conventional Peierls dimerization. This bond inversion coincides with a heat-capacity anomaly and a profound reorganization of the dielectric response with strong suppression of dielectric loss upon cooling. The BOW exhibits strongly nonlinear, frequency-dependent I-V characteristics, clockwise hysteresis, and nonvolatile memristive switching. These findings uncover an unprecedented transformation from a dynamic bond liquid to a rigid yet electrically reconfigurable BOW, establishing bond-centered electronic order as a new organizing principle for 1D quantum matter.
summary: This paper reports the discovery of an electronic Bond-Order Wave (BOW) in the quasi-1D material $	ext{Ba}_9	ext{Rh}_8	ext{O}_{24}$ below a critical temperature $T_A$. The transition is marked by a structural bond inversion, which stabilizes a rigid electronic order, evidenced by correlated anomalies in dielectric and non-linear transport measurements. This establishes bond-centered order as a novel organizing principle for correlated quantum matter.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is stabilizing collective electronic order in one dimension, a regime prone to fluctuations that suppress symmetry-breaking states.
main_result: The authors report the emergence of a Bond-Order Wave (BOW) in $	ext{Ba}_9	ext{Rh}_8	ext{O}_{24}$, characterized by a structural bond inversion at $T_A \approx 180 	ext{ K}$ and confirmed by correlated anomalies in dielectric and transport measurements.
method: The study combines single-crystal X-ray diffraction to track structural bond changes with multiple electrical and thermodynamic measurements (dielectric response, heat capacity, I-V curves) to diagnose the electronic state transition.
model_or_system: The physical system is the quasi-one-dimensional material $	ext{Ba}_9	ext{Rh}_8	ext{O}_{24}$, whose electronic behavior is modeled by considering bond-centered electronic order, which overcomes 1D fluctuations.
key_observables: Bond inversion (short $\leftrightarrow$ long Rh-Rh bonds), heat-capacity anomaly, suppression of dielectric loss ($\epsilon''$), and nonlinear/memristive I-V hysteresis.
important_parameters: Transition temperature $T_A \approx 180 	ext{ K}$; the system transitions from a dynamic bond liquid to a rigid BOW state.
main_assumptions: The observed electrical behavior is attributed to an intrinsic collective reorganization of the bond network, rather than purely thermal effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the bond inversion via X-ray diffraction, the coincidence of anomalies in heat capacity and dielectric response near $T_A$, and the development of nonvolatile memristive switching below $T_A$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically links structural evidence (bond inversion) with thermodynamic (heat capacity) and electronic transport signatures (dielectric/I-V) to establish a unified picture of the transition into a rigid BOW state.
why_interesting: The work provides an experimental realization of bond-centered electronic order, offering a platform to study correlated electron physics in low dimensions where conventional CDW or magnetic ordering might fail.
